title: An effect row reads like a small pane, with a chevron, an eye and a lit title
goal: An effect row wears a tick where the panel's other rows would have a chevron, and its title looks the same weight as the settings underneath it, so a row and its contents run together. Make an effect read like a small version of a panel section: a chevron on the left that folds its settings away, a title lit up the way a section title is but a size smaller, and the switch moved to the right as an eye beside the remove cross, matching how a layer is shown and hidden everywhere else in the app.
notes: Asked for by the user on 2026-09-08 with two screenshots of a Border row. The treatment to echo is already in the file: a panel section header draws a chevron at 10 point bold and its title with subheadline semibold (Sources/Photonz/LayersPanel.swift, the CollapsibleSection body around line 1500), so an effect header wants the same but one step smaller, and the runner should take the values from there rather than inventing new ones. The row today is built in EffectsListInspector.swift around line 89, with the switch in the ColorPartLayout.switchWidth column; moving it to the right means the row's columns change, so check the alignment work that lines the settings rule up under the left column, since the left column becomes the chevron. The eye to copy is the layer row's visibility button (LayersPanel.swift around line 2240), which uses eye and eye slash at 11 point with a tertiary tint when off. Note this partly reverses the-tick-comes-before-the-name-on-every-row-that, which asked for the tick to lead the row; that request is satisfied differently here, since the leading control becomes a chevron and the switch becomes an eye, so read that task and close or fold it rather than leaving the two fighting.
acceptance: An effect row has a chevron on its left; pressing it folds the effect's settings away and pressing again brings them back, and the state is remembered per effect while the layer stays picked
The effect's name is drawn like a panel section title, in the same weight and colour, one size smaller, so it is clearly the header of what sits under it
The tick is gone from the left; switching the effect on and off is an eye at the right of the row, beside the remove cross, drawn and behaving like the eye on a layer row
An effect switched off reads as off at a glance, and its settings can still be opened and changed while it is off
The remove cross and the reorder grip keep their places and their behaviour
Appearance's rows keep whatever they have today unless the audit argues they should follow, in which case they follow rather than diverge
The whole row is reachable from the keyboard and every control has a name a screen reader can read
Audit written under queue/audits/ with an effect open, folded, and switched off, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) Two hide-shaped controls in one row: a chevron that folds settings and an eye that stops the effect drawing. Kept them far apart, left edge and right edge, and gave the eye the layer rows exact drawing so the one that already means shown/hidden everywhere in the app keeps meaning that. (2) The mock-ish ask would have the eye at the far right like a layer row, but the checklist says the cross keeps its place, and the cross is at the panel edge today. Settled on grip, eye, cross: the cross does not move and the eye sits beside it, which is what the ask says in words. (3) Settings open while off is new, and it makes the landing swatch in the header redundant whenever the settings are showing, since the colour row is right there. So the header swatch now only appears while the settings are folded away. (4) The fold cannot be keyed to an effect identity because a LayerEffect has none: the row id is kind.index, so removing or reordering would move a fold onto the wrong effect. Folds are therefore cleared whenever the list is added to, taken from or reordered, which never looks wrong, rather than remapped, which can. (5) Shortest version: no new persistence, no launch-to-launch memory, no per-kind defaults.

Values taken from the file rather than invented: a section header is chevron.right 10pt bold secondary with a subheadline semibold title (11pt); the layers group twist is chevron.right 9pt semibold secondary. An effect header is the group twist chevron and a footnote semibold title (10pt, measured), so it is one step down the same scale. Hoisted both into PanelSectionLook so CollapsibleSection and the effect row read one place.

Built. PanelSectionLook holds the two sizes of heading in one place and CollapsibleSection now reads it. An effect heading is a chevron (9pt semibold, the layers group twist) in the column the tick used to hold, so OwnedSettings rule still hangs from it, plus a footnote semibold title in the primary ink; chevron and title are one button. The eye is the layer rows eye glyph for glyph, in the shared panel edge slot, between the grip and the cross. Fold state lives in EditorState.foldedEffectRows and is cleared on selection change and on add, remove and move.

Verified on the running probe with Screen Recording granted. New walk Scripts/playtest/effect-row-is-a-small-pane-walk.json runs green through fold, unfold, switch off, change the Width while off (4 pt to 18 pt with the eye shut), switch back on, remove. Second walk effect-eye-over-two-shapes-walk.json drives the eye over a two shape selection. Captures show the rule centred under the chevron, the folded effect keeping its lit name, and the off effect reading off by eye, title and faded settings.

Caught in a real capture and fixed: fading the settings of a switched off effect with a plain opacity let the colour wells checkerboard show through the swatch, so a solid border colour claimed to be half transparent. SwiftUI fades children one by one unless the block is flattened first; compositingGroup before opacity fixes it.

Adversarial review of the built thing. Kept: an effect eye lands one slot in from the panel edge because the cross keeps the outer place, so the eyes in Layers and the eyes in Effects are not one column. That is what the checklist asked for and it is the first question in the audit. Kept: a fold is forgotten when you pick another layer or restructure the list. Not driven: Tab through the panel, since this terminal has no Accessibility grant, so keyboard reach is claimed from the code and said so in the audit.
